 Home / Discounts / New 3-4 Day Disneyland Ticket Deals Coming for 2027 New 3-4 Day Disneyland Ticket Deals Coming for 2027
 By Tom Bricker 
 November 10, 2026 
 3 Comments 
 Disney has announced the first ticket deal of 2027 for Disneyland Resort, with discount 2-day and 3-day tickets available for the general public to purchase going on sale soon. Here are dates & details about the special offer, plus comparisons to other past & present ticket promos and more.
 First and foremost, this is good news to hear, as it’s been a relatively quiet second half of 2026 for discounts. The big recent one was the Costco Disneyland Fully Loaded 2-Day Park Hopper Ticket Deal , which was an exceptional discount offering $233 in savings. Unfortunately, it’s our understanding that deal has completely sold out. (Thanks a lot, eBay pirates!)
 Still ongoing is the Rare PIN Code Deal on 1-Day Disneyland Park Hopper Tickets . That one is still available for use from now through December 18, 2026 at a cost of $149 per day. Of course, it requires receiving the code in the first place, which is a fairly significant barrier to entry.
 Aside from those two discounts, which had fairly big asterisks attached, there hasn’t been much in the deal department for a while. In a normal year, there are a few main types of ticket deals. The big one is the winter and spring special offer, available only to Californians (usually Southern California residents). Disneyland has done this consistently for at least the last 15 years. It’s the much more established and longstanding deal.
 This year’s version of that SoCal resident deal was the best we’ve seen in a while, and was actually better than last year (which was also very good by historical standards). It started in early January and was supposed to run through May 21st. However, it was so popular that Disneyland actually stopped selling it in April because the parks ran out of reservations for that ticket type with over a month left in the promo.
 Following that, there was the $50 Disneyland Kids Tickets for Summer 2026. This was valid for visits through September 7th. With that, children ages 3 through 9 could visit Disneyland and Disney California Adventure for $50 per child with a 1-Day Park Hopper ticket.
 In addition to that Kids’ Ticket Deal, Disneyland would normally release a summer and early fall ticket discount to replace the last California resident ticket deal that ended on May 21st. In a normal year, that would expire in late September.
 For reasons unknown, that summer Golden State deal did not happen this year. Our best guess is that Disneyland overcorrected after offering “too good” of a deal in the winter and spring, and then couldn’t quickly pivot once pumping the brakes. It’s not as if Disneyland was packed with people this summer. To the contrary, the last few months have generally been much slower than the height of winter and spring.
 Instead, there was a $59 nighttime ticket deal that sold out in a single day, along with an Anaheim resident deal that is offered annually. That was followed by the aforementioned PIN code and Costco deal, which brings us to the present. Suffice to say, it’s been a really weird year for discounts at Disneyland. But we’re seeing signs that late 2026 and early 2027 are already shaping up to be better. Here’s the latest on that front…
 New 3-Day & 4-Day Disneyland Ticket Deals in 2027
 For a limited time, the general public will be able to save 20% on 3-day or 4-day Disneyland Resort tickets when booked through an Authorized Disney Vacation Planner or travel agent. This special offer goes live on December 1, 2026.
 Here’s pricing for the upcoming 2027 Disneyland Ticket deal:
 3-Day, 1-Park Ticket 
 $340 Total Price
 $113 Per Day
 Tickets are valid from January 4, 2027 and expire 13 days after first use or on May 27, 2027, whichever comes first.
 Park reservations are required.
 Sales start December 1st
 4-Day, 1-Park Ticket 
 $384 Total Price
 $96 Per Day
 Tickets are valid from January 4, 2027 and expire 13 days after first use or on May 27, 2027, whichever comes first.
 Park reservations are required.
 Sales start December 1st
 2027 Disneyland Ticket Deal Analysis
 When it comes to assessing the value proposition, I’m going to compare this to the Summer 2025 deal, which was the last comparable 3-4 day special offer for the general public. There have been better deals since, like the aforementioned Costco or California resident ones, but they’ve each had their own (big) barriers to entry. That was the last with minimal hoops that the general public could purchase.
 That deal started right as Disneyland’s 70th Anniversary began. It was priced at $360 for the 3-day version or $400 for the 4-day version. Obviously, this is cheaper than that despite being released two price increase cycles later. That’s the good!
 The bad is that Disney overpriced that deal, overestimating demand for the 70th entertainment. As a result, the months after the anniversary started were actually less busy than the months before, when there was an incredibly aggressive resident ticket deal (historical deals listed below for reference). There’s also the practical reality that winter and spring deals are always less expensive than summer ones.
 On balance, this new 2027 special offer is neither the best nor the worst ticket deal we’ve seen from Disneyland in recent years. Despite there being much better targeted offers in the last two years, it’s still fairly middle of the road once you account for the hassles that came with those. At minimum, it’s reassuring to see something  for the general public; we’ll take the sure thing with no friction!
 2027 Disneyland Ticket Deal: Where to Buy
 Our recommended authorized third party ticket seller, Get Away Today , will be selling these discounted tickets once they’re released on December 1, 2026. Also worth noting is that Get Away Today is currently running their early Black Friday deals, which include Adults at Kids’ prices along with hotel and ticket bundle deals.
 If you’re planning on doing a hotel stay to take advantage of the stackable savings, our advice would be booking now and changing ticket types once this deal is released. Get Away Today allows you to modify your tickets without penalty if/when a better deal is released, so it’s always advantageous to book earlier rather than later. This will be true again on December 1, 2026 once this ticket offer goes live, but the other Black Friday deals have ended.
 With the core details out of the way, here’s some of the relevant fine print, most of which is the standard (but important) language about Disneyland using separate ‘buckets’ of reservations for this ticket deal versus full-priced admission…
 2027 Disneyland Ticket Deal Fine Print
 Tickets valid for use beginning January 4, 2027 and expire 13 days after the first day of use or on May 27, 2027, whichever occurs first. Guests must make a park reservation for the first theme park they wish to visit to begin their day; the ability to visit the other park will be subject to that park’s capacity limitations, operational hours, closures and other restrictions, and is not guaranteed.
 Tickets are nonrefundable, may not be sold or transferred for commercial use and exclude activities/events separately priced. Offer may not be combined with other ticket discounts or promotions. Subject to restrictions and change or cancellation without notice. Sales may be paused from time to time or terminated at any time.
 Lightning Lane passes, attractions and arrival windows included with this service are limited in availability and are not guaranteed, may vary by date, are subject to change or closure, and may not be available at all on the date of visit or at the time of selection or redemption. Availability can change throughout the day. To enter a park, both a theme park reservation and a valid ticket for the same park on the same date are required.
 Theme park reservations for 3-Day and 4-Day Disneyland 2027 Ticket Special Offer holders are limited in number and subject to the availability of park reservations allocated to the 3-Day and 4-Day Disneyland 2027 Ticket Special Offer as determined by Disney and theme park capacity.
 Reservation availability for 3-Day and 4-Day Disneyland 2027 Ticket Special Offer holders is not guaranteed for any date, and reservations may be difficult to get for any particular date, especially as the ticket expiration date approaches. To ensure best availability, make reservations early.
 On any given date, park reservations may be available for general theme park tickets even though park reservations allocated to the Special 3 Day Disneyland Ticket Offer are fully reserved. Special 3 Day Disneyland Ticket Offer holders are not entitled to any reservations Disney makes available to others. Check park reservation availability by visiting StartYourDisneylandExperience.com prior to purchase.

 Ultimately, this 3-Day and 4-Day Disneyland 2027 Ticket Special Offer is a decent deal as far as general public promos go. If you want shorter or longer duration tickets, live in California, or want the various add-ons, there are probably going to be better alternatives for you, though.
 For those who are wondering, we fully expect this to supplement as opposed to replace the standard Southern California resident discount in early 2027. We anticipate that will be announced right around the time this deal is released, in early December (as has been the case the last couple of years). But we also expected a summer and early fall discount and doubled-down on that prediction a few times, so nothing is certain.
 The material difference is that the winter is still the off-season for tourism to California (even as travel trends shift, this remains generally true), and Disneyland is reliant upon locals to pick up the slack. Not only that, but whereas the summer ticket deals are a post-COVID phenomenon, the winter and spring deal has been offered to residents every single year since we’ve been covering this stuff, and likely long before that.
 What this new 3-4 day ticket deal probably does is confirms that the big winter and spring deal will be residents-only, as opposed to expanding to the general public. It also sets the bar for the resident deal, as that will almost assuredly be cheaper than this. At the same time, we wouldn’t expect the 2027 resident deal to be anywhere nearly as good as this year’s version. That deal was a little too good for its own good (and the guest experience as a whole).
 Regardless, it’s great to see another discount, which is doubly true given the dearth of discounts over the last six-plus months. It would appear that Disneyland is getting back on track with deals, setting the table for another strong Southern California resident offer in Winter 2027. We’ll keep you posted!

 Will you be taking advantage of the new 3-Day and 4-Day Disneyland 2027 Ticket Special Offer once it’s released in December? Or are you waiting for the California resident deal, and hoping for something on par with last year’s deep discounts? Do you agree or disagree with our assessment? Any questions?
